report.source_text: He was placed on long-term steroid therapy of Prednisolone . He responded very well to his recent course of steroids. His rash completely cleared. There have been no further flares. His shoulder pain also settled. He was scheduled for regular follow ups.

clinician.trajectory_summary: A 76-year-old man with a 5-year history of intermittent erythematous, granulomatous, discoid plaques rash on trunk, arms, and back accompanied by normocytic anemia, thrombocytopenia, and elevated inflammatory markers underwent a skin biopsy showing a superficial dermal inflammatory infiltrate with histiocyte-like cells and neutrophils suggestive of Sweet's syndrome or interstitial granulomatous dermatitis. Subsequent genetic testing identified a pathogenic UBA1 gene variant with a variant allele frequency of 27.7%, confirming VEXAS syndrome. The patient was treated with long-term prednisolone, resulting in complete clearance of the rash and resolution of shoulder pain with no further flares.
